Data integrity and provenance [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Protects training, validation, test, fine-tuning and retrieval data against unauthorised or malicious modification (poisoning, label manipulation, backdoor insertion) and makes the provenance of every data item used to build or ground the model traceable. Levels: 1 Documented provenance; 2 Controlled datasets; 3 Poisoning-resistant pipeline; 4 Attested provenance.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Documented provenance): The data-governance policy defines the set of datasets (training, validation, test, fine-tuning, retrieval corpora) to which it applies. For each dataset the source, collection method, licence, pre-processing and labelling steps and intended use are documented (datasheet). A content manifest with cryptographic digests is produced for every dataset version used to build an evaluated model. Level 2 (Controlled datasets): The policy applies to all datasets used by the AI system. Datasets are versioned under configuration management; integrity is verified against the manifest before each training or evaluation run. Only authorised roles can modify datasets; every modification is recorded in a protected log. Level 3 (Poisoning-resistant pipeline): Sources of externally acquired data are authenticated. Statistical screening for poisoned, mislabelled and anomalous samples is applied before training. The effectiveness of screening is demonstrated in a poisoning drill at the declared budget beta. Level 4 (Attested provenance): Every transformation from raw source to training set produces signed provenance attestations verifiable by a third party. The influence of any k training samples is bounded by a certified method, or the poisoning drill is repeated by an independent party with adaptive strategies.

description: Adversarial robustness [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Ensures that the AI system maintains its declared performance under adversarially manipulated inputs within a declared threat model (perturbation set, attacker knowledge, query budget), including evasion of predictive models and prompt injection or jailbreaking of generative models. Levels: 1 Declared threat model and black-box assessment; 2 Adaptive white-box robustness; 3 Certified or architecturally enforced robustness; 4 Runtime adversarial resilience.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Declared threat model and black-box assessment): The robustness policy declares the threat model (perturbation set Delta, attacker knowledge, query budget Q) for the declared operational domain. Robustness is assessed with transfer-based and query-based black-box attacks; attack success is reported with a confidence interval. Level 2 (Adaptive white-box robustness): Robustness is evaluated with adaptive white-box attacks tailored to the deployed defences within Delta. Mitigations are documented and evaluated against adaptive attacks; obscurity is not credited. Level 3 (Certified or architecturally enforced robustness): Predictive models carry a certified robustness guarantee over the declared region (e.g., randomized smoothing or formal verification). Generative or agentic systems separate trusted instructions from untrusted content architecturally so that injected content cannot trigger privileged actions. Level 4 (Runtime adversarial resilience): Adversarial inputs are detected or contained in operation; detections raise alarms and trigger a safe or degraded mode. Robustness regression tests gate every model update; independent red-teaming is repeated periodically.

description: Validity and reliability [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Ensures that outputs are valid for the intended purpose within the declared operational domain (accuracy, calibration, robustness to natural shift, factual grounding) and that the system detects and signals operation outside that domain. Levels: 1 Declared performance; 2 Statistically assured performance; 3 Operating-envelope monitoring; 4 Continuous validation.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Declared performance): The intended purpose, operational domain and performance metrics are declared. Performance is measured on held-out data representative of the operational domain and reported with confidence intervals. Level 2 (Statistically assured performance): Each declared metric is accepted on held-out test data, not used for development or model selection, whose size is not smaller than n_min(alpha_G, delta). Performance is reported for declared operating conditions and subgroups; calibration is measured where outputs are probabilistic. Level 3 (Operating-envelope monitoring): Inputs outside the declared operational domain and data or concept drift are detected with declared thresholds; the system abstains, flags or degrades safely. Uncertainty is quantified with coverage guarantees where applicable (e.g., conformal prediction). Level 4 (Continuous validation): Online performance monitoring uses statistically controlled alarms and an automatic fallback to a safe state on validated degradation. Generative systems apply grounding or factuality controls with a measured confabulation rate. The system is re-validated before every model update.

description: Explainability and transparency [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Enables users, operators and evaluators to understand the capabilities, limitations and individual outputs of the AI system to the extent necessary for appropriate use and oversight. Levels: 1 System transparency; 2 Decision-level explanation; 3 Verifiable interpretability.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (System transparency): A model or system card states the intended purpose, capabilities, limitations, declared performance and known risks; instructions for use are provided. Interaction with AI and AI-generated content are disclosed where applicable. Level 2 (Decision-level explanation): Each output relevant to oversight is accompanied by an explanation (attribution, counterfactual or retrieved evidence) available to the operator and recorded with the decision. Explanation fidelity is measured against ground truth or perturbation tests and compared with a declared trivial explainer (e.g., a constant or random explainer), whose accuracy the threshold must exceed. Level 3 (Verifiable interpretability): Decisions of the highest declared criticality are produced by an inherently interpretable model or by methods with formal fidelity guarantees. Explanations are reproducible from logged inputs and support contestation.

description: Bias management [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Identifies, measures and mitigates harmful statistical, systemic and human-cognitive bias in data and outputs for groups relevant to the intended purpose. Levels: 1 Bias identification; 2 Quantified group parity; 3 Intersectional and operational bias monitoring.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Bias identification): Groups and attributes relevant to the intended purpose are identified; datasets are analysed for representativeness; bias risks are documented. Level 2 (Quantified group parity): Declared fairness metrics are measured with confidence intervals; mitigations are documented. Level 3 (Intersectional and operational bias monitoring): Intersectional disparities are analysed; disparities are monitored in operation with alarm thresholds; causal analysis is documented where feasible.

description: Inference-attack protection [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Protects training data and model functionality against inference through model access: membership and attribute inference, model inversion, training-data extraction and model extraction (stealing). Levels: 1 Exposure minimisation; 2 Empirical leakage testing; 3 Formal privacy guarantee; 4 Privacy-preserving architecture.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Exposure minimisation): Personal or sensitive training data are minimised and pseudonymised; outputs are minimised to what the purpose requires (e.g., labels instead of scores). A model-access policy defines who may query the model and how. Level 2 (Empirical leakage testing): State-of-the-art membership-inference tests are run where the training data contain personal or confidential records, and training-data extraction tests for generative models; model-extraction resistance is tested at the declared query budget Q on a declared evaluation distribution. Query volume and rate are limited per identity; queries are logged. Level 3 (Formal privacy guarantee): Training satisfies differential privacy with declared (epsilon, delta) and audited accounting, or an equivalent formal guarantee. Anomalous query patterns indicative of extraction are detected and alarmed. Level 4 (Privacy-preserving architecture): Sensitive training or inference runs in confidential computing with remote attestation or in federated learning with secure aggregation. An independent privacy audit confirms that empirical leakage is consistent with the declared guarantee.

description: Human oversight [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Enables natural persons to effectively oversee the AI system in use, to interpret its outputs, to remain aware of automation bias and to intervene, override or stop the system. Levels: 1 Human-on-the-loop; 2 Human-in-the-loop for designated decisions; 3 Verified dual control.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Human-on-the-loop): Oversight roles are assigned; operators can monitor outputs and system status, disregard or override outputs and stop the system safely. Oversight measures are documented in the instructions for use. Level 2 (Human-in-the-loop for designated decisions): Outputs of declared criticality take effect only after human confirmation. Oversight workload is bounded and measured; automation-bias countermeasures (training, uncertainty cues) are documented. Level 3 (Verified dual control): Decisions of the highest declared criticality require independent verification by at least two competent persons. Oversight effectiveness is measured in drills (correct interventions, time to intervene).

description: Model integrity and supply chain [class-I AI service]. Purpose: Ensures that models and AI components, including third-party and foundation models, libraries and serialised artefacts, are authentic, unmodified and of known provenance throughout the life cycle. Levels: 1 Component inventory; 2 Signed artefacts; 3 Attested lineage.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Component inventory): A model card and an AI bill of materials list models, datasets, libraries and base or foundation models with versions and origins. Listed components are monitored for published vulnerabilities. Level 2 (Signed artefacts): Model artefacts and the AI bill of materials are cryptographically signed; signatures and digests are verified at load time against a trust anchor held outside the signed artefacts (a pinned key or a certificate of the platform PKI). Serialisation formats that execute code on load are prohibited or scanned. Level 3 (Attested lineage): Build-provenance attestations link data, code and configuration to each model. Third-party models are accepted only with provenance attestation and backdoor scanning.

description: Agency bounding [class-I AI service]. Purpose: For AI systems able to invoke tools or take actions (agentic systems), bounds the set, scope and impact of actions to the authorised objective under complete mediation. Levels: 1 Declared action space; 2 Least-agency mediation; 3 Reference-monitor mediation.
levels_or_first_required: Level 1 (Declared action space): Tools, actions, parameters and permitted targets are declared in an allow-list. Every action is logged with its triggering context; iteration, resource and spending limits are enforced. Level 2 (Least-agency mediation): Each action is authorised under least privilege with delegated, not elevated, identity; untrusted content cannot trigger privileged actions without confirmation. High-impact actions require human approval; tool execution is sandboxed. Level 3 (Reference-monitor mediation): All agent actions are mediated by a tamper-proof, always-invoked and verifiable policy-enforcement point implementing a formalised policy. Complete mediation is tested by an independent party; agent actions can be halted and, where possible, rolled back.
